> Combine several independent p-values for each feature into one, by Fisher's or Stouffer's method, optionally weighted and optionally signed by each test's effect.

Wire verb `stats combine-p` · Python [`pymzlib.stats.combine_p`][pymzlib.stats.combine_p]

### Wraps

- [`PValueCombination.Fisher`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`PValueCombination.Stouffer`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`PValueCombination.OneSided`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`
- [`CombinedPValue`](https://github.com/smith-chem-wisc/mzLib/blob/d10017ce/mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs) in `mzLib/StatisticalModels/PValueCombination.cs` at mzLib `d10017ce`

### Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Unit | Range | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` | required | — | `fisher \| stouffer` | The combination rule. REQUIRED: mzLib has the two as separate methods and prefers neither, so the bridge picks none. fisher is PValueCombination.Fisher, Fisher (1925): X = -2 sum ln p, referred to chi-square with 2k degrees of freedom; it is driven by the smallest p-values and takes no weights. stouffer is PValueCombination.Stouffer, Stouffer et al. (1949): Z = sum w z / sqrt(sum w^2) with z = the standard normal quantile of 1 - p, referred to N(0, 1); it weighs every test. |
| `stdin` | `string[]` | required | — | `>= 1 line of 2 to 4 tab-separated fields` | One test per line, tab-separated: feature, p_value, then optionally weight and effect. No header; blank lines are skipped; a UTF-8 BOM is dropped. A feature's lines need not be adjacent: features are reported in order of first appearance, and each is combined by its own mzLib call. p_value is a fraction in [0, 1]; a blank, NA or NaN p_value is a test that could not be run, which mzLib omits. weight (stouffer only; a positive number, for example the square root of the study's sample size) must be on every line or on none; a blank or NA third field is no weight. effect (the test's estimate, any unit: only its sign is used) must be a fourth field on every line or on none. With effects, each p_value is read as TWO-SIDED and converted by PValueCombination.OneSided to the one-sided p-value for effect > 0 (p/2 for a positive effect, 1 - p/2 for a negative one) before combining; an effect that is 0, blank, NA or NaN has no direction, so mzLib returns NaN and the test is omitted. Write feature, p, a blank weight and the effect to give an effect without a weight. |

### Returns

Top-level fields:

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | `string` | — | never | fisher \| stouffer, as given. |
| `weighted` | `bool` | — | never | Whether the lines carried weights (stouffer only). |
| `signed` | `bool` | — | never | Whether the lines carried effects, so each p-value was read as two-sided and converted to the one-sided p-value for effect > 0. |
| `line_count` | `int` | lines | never | Test lines read from stdin, over every feature. |
| `feature_count` | `int` | features | never | Distinct features; the table's row count. |
| `row_count` | `int` | rows | never | Equal to feature_count. |
| `column_names` | `string[]` | — | never | The table's columns, in order. |
| `columns` | `table` | — | never | One row per feature, in order of first appearance. |
| `caveats` | `string[]` | — | never | Three static caveats, plus: two when signed (one only for fisher), and one each when any test was omitted (with the count), when a feature has nothing left to combine, when a feature holds both a p-value of 0 and of 1 (stouffer), and when a statistic is infinite. |

Per-row fields (one value per record, in `columns` or each list entry):

| Field | Type | Unit | Null? | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `feature` | `string` | — | never | As given on stdin. |
| `studies` | `int` | tests | never | Tests combined: mzLib's CombinedPValue.Studies, the finite p-values after any signed conversion. |
| `omitted` | `int` | tests | never | This feature's lines that were not combined: a blank, NA or NaN p_value, or (signed) an effect that is 0, blank, NA or NaN. studies + omitted is the feature's line count. |
| `statistic` | `float` | fisher: chi-square statistic on 2 x studies degrees of freedom; stouffer: standard normal deviates | yes: not finite. With studies 0, nothing was combined (p_value null too). Otherwise p_value says which: 0 means plus infinity (a p-value of 0 among the tests), 1 means minus infinity (stouffer, a p-value of 1), and null means undefined (stouffer, a p-value of 0 and one of 1 together) | Fisher's X = -2 sum ln p, or Stouffer's Z = sum w z / sqrt(sum w^2). |
| `p_value` | `float` | fraction (0 to 1) | yes: studies is 0 (nothing to combine), or stouffer met a p-value of 0 and one of 1 (z of plus and minus infinity) | Combined p-value: the UPPER tail of the statistic's reference distribution, so it tests one direction (effect > 0 when signed). Fisher's is the regularized upper incomplete gamma Q(k, X/2), so a tiny value keeps its digits. Not adjusted across features. |

### Errors

| Kind | pyMzLib raises | When |
|---|---|---|
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | --method missing, given without a value, or not fisher or stouffer; stdin empty; a line with fewer than 2 or more than 4 tab-separated fields; an empty feature name; a p_value, weight or effect that is not a number (other than blank, NA, NaN) |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | a weight on some lines and not others; an effect field on some lines and not others; any weight with --method fisher |
| `usage` | [`UsageError`][pymzlib.UsageError] | mzLib refuses a feature's input, named in the message: a p-value outside [0, 1], or a weight that is not finite and positive (mzLib's ArgumentException, reclassified) |
| `correctness` | [`BridgeError`][pymzlib.BridgeError] | never expected |
| `service_unavailable` | [`ServiceUnavailableError`][pymzlib.ServiceUnavailableError] | never raised by this verb |

### Caveats

- Both rules assume the tests are independent and test the same one-sided hypothesis. Fisher is driven by the smallest p-values; Stouffer weighs every test, and with weights (for example the square root of each study's sample size) lets larger studies count more.
- p_value is the upper tail of the statistic, so it tests one direction. Two-sided p-values given without their effects are combined as if one-sided, and opposite effects then reinforce each other instead of cancelling: give each test's effect for that.
- Neither rule estimates an effect size; pool the estimates with stats meta for that. p_value is not adjusted across features; send the p_value column to stats adjust.
- Signed: p_value tests effect > 0, and for stouffer a p_value near 1 means a consistently negative effect. mzLib computes no two-sided combined p-value. For a negative effect whose two-sided p-value is below about 2e-16, 1 - p/2 rounds to 1, so that test's z is minus infinity and decides a stouffer feature (p_value 1).

### Example

```python
combined = pymzlib.stats.combine_p([(r['case'], float(r['p'])) for r in rows], method='fisher')
```
